chapter: Opening and the Buddy Petit band
title: Buddy Petit compared with Kid Rene, Evan Thomas and Louis Armstrong
summary: Petit contrasted with high-note player Rene, Evan Thomas and Louis Armstrong; Zardis recalls Bunk and Baker duets and says all respected Petit.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: How did Buddy compare say with Kid Rene? I mean were there styles anything the same or different?

No, there was a different style. Different style altogether. Well both of them boys was tough. They were two good men. But Rene, he was a high man. Yeah, he played high notes. And Rene played something like this boy, Yvonne Thomas. You ever heard of Yvonne Thomas?
Well I've heard about him. Bunk used to talk about him.
Yeah well that's a tough man too. That's a tough man.
In Crowley and New Iberia and all that section.

And you take Bunk, I mean that Bunk, this boy Yvonne, and we used to have a tenor player called Baker. You know? You ever met Baker? No, never met Baker. That's two men. Well I mean we used to work together. I mean duets, you know what I mean? Both of them up there high, trumpet high and that clarinet right under there, playing the same thing. Ours was pretty.
Well how did Buddy compare with Louis Armstrong would you say?

Well Louis, he wasn't the man Louis. I mean Buddy wasn't the man Louis, you know what I mean? But all of them respected Buddy. All of them, because Buddy could play. Buddy used to play. Like I tell you before, he never played those high notes. Yeah I know everybody's told me he was wonderful. But what he played in that staff and down below that staff make you swim in the head. Oh yeah, so much stuff. And then he had a nice springboard. Oh yeah, he had a nice springboard.
